[Marginal note: Paracelsus, book on the resuscitation of natural things, fol. 295.] For no Remedy can vindicate a corruptible body from death, the punishment and wages of sins: but there is one thing which removes corruption, renews youth, and prolongs a brief life as in the Patriarchs. However, hesitation of Belief & distrust not only dissipate & break the virtue of the working mind, which is the middle ground between both extremes, but also weaken every work, both in Superstition, & in true Religion, & enervate the desired effect, even of the strongest Experiments: And what should be diligently noted in this place, our Savior, as the sacred Page teaches, in Capernaum οὐκ ἐδυνάτο (was not able) to perform miracles, because they did not believe, & resisted Him with their unbelief and false faith. For just as Man can do nothing without God, so God in turn wills nothing without Man, as His instrument; God & Creature both together, neither without the other. Therefore, no one ought to will without God, because no one can exist without God, in whom we are, live, & move.

EIGHTH. Lest a recovering sick person commit greater sins against God, his neighbor, and himself, with the loss of his soul, inasmuch as every illness is an expiation, or by this divine innate punishment, vengeance, and scourge he is called by the just judge to the amendment of life in the future. Or by this Paternal visitation, and the cross patiently to be borne, let him be an example to himself and his neighbor, to a more ardent Fear and worship of GOD, because God often permits certain men to fall into many and great illnesses, for whom a joyful health of the flesh, with the continuation of sins, would have brought the greatest illness of the mind, not without the loss of eternal salvation. For health without the remission of sins profits nothing, since it is rather a condemnation. Moreover, sins weaken the powers of the Soul, so that it is powerless for the Natural Governance of the body: Therefore the powers of the body are weakened and hasten to death.

Paracelsus calls diseases "Deales" (Divine) from the Being of God, who inflicts all such diseases, and alone works through good and bad. He says that healing happens by Faith, or after purgatory is finished, finally a cure is to be attempted by medicines. From which arises Old Age, the house of oblivion; finally follows the complete extinction, consumption, and dissipation of that spirit, which is Natural Death. Therefore, so that the consumption and dissipation of the said spirit (as far as is permitted by Nature) may be avoided, that spirit and heat, existing naturally in human bodies, thus diminished or impeded, must be increased and strengthened, so that it may perform its office more strongly and better.

But when every agent begins to act, it does not move to something inferior to itself, but to its equal, its like, and that which is agreeable to it: This strengthening must also be done by its like, namely by that Celestial Heat of the Sun and Moon, and other Planets, or with those things in which the Virtue of the Sun and Moon
[Marginal note:] The spirit of the world or Celestial and the Natural spirit of our body is one and the same spirit: Therefore, the Heat of the Sun and Moon, generated from the very impulse of the spirit, is a more digested thing, and consequently more perfect.
is most powerful, and most abundant, and is less inhibited by matter: For these things act more quickly and perfectly, and more readily generate their like: Indeed, that from these things, the spirit or that supernal Fire is also more easily elicited by artifice: whose properties are Heat, not burning like the Elemental, but fertilizing all things, and Light giving life to all. But the properties of Elemental and Inferior Fire are burning Heat, consuming all things, and darkness filling all with sterility.

Therefore, this one is excluded, and along with it all diverse or contrary things, such as all Inferior Elements. For these and all other things, which

include in themselves a Natural composition (insofar
as, still immersed in coarser matter, they are not yet
separated from it) are subject to corruption and transmutation:
Preservative medicines, however, ought to be very
durable, and removed from corruption: For since they
ought to preserve the Human body from corruption, they
must first of all be durable, otherwise they would corrupt
more than they would preserve. I add, that it would be
vain to wish to preserve a corruptible body by means of
a putrid and corruptible thing. To heal the weak by means
of a weak thing, to form a thing by means of a thing [Marginal note 1]
subject to deformity. For every corruptible, weak, and
feeble thing added to its like, increases it, and thus that
corruptibility is augmented, and not diminished, as we
see many, and indeed very many, physicians of our age
try in vain to render a Human being healthy and immune
from diseases with their coarse and corporeal compositions
of medicines: For a deeper speculation is required here:
For diseases, since they are not corporeal but spiritual,
as they lie hidden in the spirits, also demand spiritual [Marginal note 2]
medicines. Therefore, for those wishing to preserve that
vital spirit in youths (which is the radical moist and
warm, the innate Mumia, and has its seat in the middle
of the Human heart, as the support of all our life), and
in the elderly, to restore it when languishing, and as it
were to bring them back to youth, as to their strength,
and thus to bring the life of Man to the highest health,

Paracelsus: The Tincture so purifies the Balsam that even hereditary offspring in the tenth generation may feel the effect of health.

This will be the duty of a true physician and a sounder philosopher: For thus he could preserve our body without corruption, retard old age, retain flourishing youth in vigor even to the very end of life, and, were it not for the wages of sin obstructing it, he could preserve it in eternal health and protect it from destruction. Paracelsus calls the Element FIRE, which, like a Terrestrial sun or an inferior Firmament, becomes the supreme Arcanum in removing all diseases and reviving cold, dead limbs. For that Essential Fire operates in the body like a Flame, and outside the body like a nettle. [Large decorative initial V with floral and foliage motifs] WOULD that the botanists of our time, who, ignorant of the internal form, know at least the matter, substance, and body of Herbs, would apply as diligent care in discerning the Signatures of Plants as they do accurate (care) in their various and often frivolous contentions about names; a far richer and more fruitful utility would thence redound to the Medical Commonwealth. 6          PRAEFATIO
...in all external things, the house is at least the dwelling place of internal virtues, infused by God like the Soul into the human body. More correctly, that Philosopher sought the minds and senses of men not from their name, but from their speech (the character and true indication of the mind or inner Man), while he thus addressed a silent boy standing by: 'Speak, so that I may see you, O youth, since by voice as interpreter the secret movements of the mind are revealed.' Thus Herbs magically, through Signature, address the Physician who deeply observes them, and manifest their inner parts, hidden in the secret silence of Nature, to him through similitude. For it is (to use the words of the most famous man, Baptista Porta) a way of demonstrating through similitude, by which very often the supreme Maker of Things is accustomed to reveal divine and hidden things, so that they might bear the supreme similitude of Ideas; nor could it be in a more excellent or more fitting way. For if we imagine a plant speaking, and wishing to reveal the secret advantages of its Nature, by which it excels, by whatever speech or in whatever ways it were to speak, it would not be perceived by all, since both speeches and writing characters are proper and peculiar to individual nations; whence it would have been necessary to speak either to one nation, or in infinite languages. Thus the keen ingenuity of Nature, by its similitudes of things, both briefly and clearly
                                        ...

DE SIGNATVRIS. 7
thus the keen ingenuity of Nature, through the similitudes of things, makes it briefly and clearly enough for everyone at once. All herbs, flowers, trees, and other things originating from the Earth, are books and magical signs, communicated by the immense mercy of God, not that those signs are our medicine, but that through the knowledge of them we can come to true medicine, that is, to the thing signified. Whoever therefore desires to be an experienced physician and has knowledge of those things which pertain to him, through that art which nature externally proposes through signs, let him recognize what it internally signifies: For everything that is intrinsic bears the external figure of that hidden thing, both in sensible and in insensible Creatures.

While we are silent, Nature speaks as if with certain signs, and reveals the character and manners of each, as it was skillfully said by Adamantius Polemon's paraphraser, σιγών των μδὺ ἔσιν ἀπόκρισις. λαλεῖ δέ οἷον τοῖς σημείοις ἡ φύσις τῶν τρόπες ἑκάσου ἀνακαλύπτουσα: (While they are silent, there is no answer; but Nature speaks, as it were, by signs, revealing the characters of each.) And just as our innermost manners can be investigated from the external marks of the body: so from the external signs of Plants, Man can be admonished of their internal powers; For a Plant, as if with hidden words, reveals its powers to sick mortals, and the treasures of hidden things, so that Man, most miserable of all, may learn how he can bring help to his diseases. 88 ON SIGNATURES
...times, holding a small stone with their foot, which, if loosened by sleep and falling, might expose their carelessness; They choose a leader who may cry out while the flocks sleep: while flying, they alternately have those positioned in the rear who may cry out and keep the flock together with their voice; when they descend to the ground, the leader cries out loudly so that all may gather and feed together, but if he becomes hoarse from too much shouting, another will be substituted. When they travel, because of the keenness of their senses, they form a triangle so that they may cut through the opposing air more easily; then gradually from both sides, as if with oars, so with their wings they lighten the course of their flight: if the sky rages and wind arises, they do not fly head-on (but they fly in a crescent-shaped globe formation when it is calm), but they move themselves into a wedge formation; if they foresee themselves being attacked by an Eagle, they stand in a circle, and, scythe-like, as if arranged in battle array, they present the appearance of a fight, wherefore the Eagle retreats; in flight, allowing (others) to rest their necks on the backs of those flying ahead (which Deer also do when swimming across rivers), they make the labor easy, and the first, becoming tired, begins to be the last; when they stop, the others sleep; the leader, keeping watch, signifies with his voice whatever he perceives. In a similar manner, the Goose performs nocturnal watches and constantly testifies to its vigils with song.

The construction of wagons; from Mice, who, lying on their backs with their four feet extended, form a cart to be loaded by others with provisions for future necessity, and afterwards to be dragged into a cave's granary with their tail serving as a pole; therefore, in Autumn, they always have a smooth back.

The same clever foresight is observed in the Beaver (an amphibious animal), who builds houses for itself on river banks with some steps and multiple levels, so that as the river water rises, it ascends, and as it falls, it descends. The tree which it chose to cut down, for the building of its house and for food, it does not leave until it has completely cut it apart with its fiercest and sharpest teeth, and when it is near falling, it looks up with each bite, lest it be unexpectedly crushed.    Physicians and Surgeons have learned very many Remedies for Diseases and Virtues of Things from Brute Animals, in whom there is Natural Skill, and an innate Medicinal Art.

   Deer have taught [us about] the herb Dittany, useful for extracting arrows; likewise, they have taught how to remove a nail fixed and adhering in the sole of the foot. Indeed, when struck by a poisoned dart, they expel and shake out the dart by feeding on that herb.

   Wild Goats have shown Surgeons the Cure for Abscesses: which wander in the mountains, and feed especially on fragrant herbs and Nard; in these [animals], blood putrefies within the skin and flesh; the pus conceived, before the abscess breaks, naturally tends towards maturation, and when this has been reached, the animal, irritated by the harmful stinging of the tickling humor, rubs itself with great pleasure against rocks and stones glowing from long exposure to the sun, until, an outlet for the abscess having been made, the entire force of the pus is discharged from the follicle onto the stones, not otherwise than an abscess with matured pus.

Jurists have observed a judicial assembly among Storks, who punish adultery with death, like lions. Hermetic Adept Philosophers learned the method of Renewing Youth from the Halcyon, Eagle, Crab, Serpents, etc., who almost annually, having shed their old skins, renew their age and become young again: For if we see this granted to brute animals, why would it not be possible for Man, created in the Image of GOD, and intelligent?

The Eagle, by shedding its feathers, lays aside old age and recovers youth.

Serpents abandon their membrane in springtime, and another is reborn; and while they are renewed, they even provide for Deer, that they may be renewed, and are effective for the renewal of our body and retard old age. For provident Nature shows, as already said, that there are very many living things (such as Serpents and Lizards, among marine creatures, Lobsters, Shrimps, and Crabs) which in spring and autumn shed old age, and put off their annual crust, admonishing man that the quality they themselves possess, namely for the peeling or renewal of the skin, will be beneficial to him.

Men, moved and excited by the examples and wisdom of these brute animals, also for their own benefit, have investigated said living beings, which in many ways resist the haste of dying and prolong their life through natural industry, so that they might know the powers of Herbs and Stones and Metals, and other things, by which they might afterwards rectify their bodies in many ways, as if miraculously.
Roger Bacon relates that once a certain wise man sought a serpent, and having found it, cut it into small pieces, with the skin of its belly nevertheless remaining intact, upon which it could crawl; that serpent, as best it could, crawled to a certain herb, by the touch of which it was immediately healed; and the experimenter thence gathered the herb of admirable virtue, because human Reason, excited by such examples of brute animals, can devise better ways and surpass all bestial Prudence.

The ant, a most industrious little animal, has that promise implanted in all of Nature, that after completing its course, it may come to a better state and have complete rest, towards which it strives with every effort. Therefore, with unceasing labors, it yearns for old age, since in old age, by a wonderful and most worthy of consideration metamorphosis, Nature creates wings for it, for the solace and recompense of its past labors, and suddenly makes it a flying fly from a little animal.

Thus also we see the Silkworm (hatched from a very tiny seed by the benefit of the spring Sun), an abject and deformed worm, die after its task is completed, and after putrefaction, having cast off the former coverings of the crawling worm, to be transformed into a lively and flying butterfly and to rise again as a butterfly.

*I beseech You, by Your ineffable Clemency of Charity, to bring it about that the Prayer and Action of all who labor to fear You heartily and with utmost zeal in Newness of life through daily mortification and complete self-abnegation, and to religiously observe Your commandments, through Your Grace, according to the love of Neighbor in this infirmity of the Flesh (since in this malignant world this is the most true Worship of God)* [Marginal note: *Eccles. 12. / sect. 13.*] [Marginal note: *Act. 10.*]

INTERNIS RERVM. 101

COROLLARY.

[Large decorative initial A] The most ancient wise men, whom we call Philosophers in the Greek tongue, if they had discovered any Secrets of Nature or Art, lest they should come into the knowledge of the wicked, concealed them in various ways and figures; [Marginal note: See the Hieroglyphic Monad of John Dee of London.]
In the same way, Hermetic Philosophers were accustomed to designate Terrestrial Planets with certain Hieroglyphic signs, by which they would, as it were, expose their latent powers or virtues to be contemplated, before the eyes of intelligent and discerning sons of art: However, so that such signs might be preserved from destruction or burial, I have judged that I would be doing a worthwhile work if, together with the Characters of other Minerals devised by Provident Antiquity to keep the Profane and unworthy Vulgar away from this study, they are now communicated by me in one work for the benefit of Hermetic disciples and the Chymical Republic.
